benefits.name: Life and Accidental Insurance
benefits.details: All employees are covered by life insurance. In case of death or disability retirement of an employee, the beneficiary receives up to 3 times of your CTC.

benefits.name: Paternity leave
benefits.details: In addition to maternity leave, male employees are entitled to paternity leave benefit of 28 calendar days. Adoption is covered up to 12 years of age, too.

benefits.name: Health and Wellness
benefits.details: To encourage physical activity and improved morale, we provide annual wellness stipends for gym memberships, health checkups, meditation sessions and more.

benefits.name: Thoughtworker Support Program
benefits.details: We provide free, 24/7 counseling services (mental, physical, financial, etc.) and referrals for Thoughtworkers and family members to help manage day-to-day life challenges.

benefits.name: Sabbatical leave
benefits.details: Upon completing ten years at Thoughtworks, an employee is entitled to 12 weeks of paid leave. For every additional five years with the company, they are entitled to six weeks of paid leave.

benefits.name: Maternity leave
benefits.details: We offer maternity leave for both biological and adoptive mothers. Supporting a smooth transition back to work is important to us, which is why we offer flexible work options once maternity leave ends.

benefits.name: Medical Insurance
benefits.details: We aid our employees and their dependents with hospitalization benefits including COVID-19 home care support. We offer coverage for members belonging to the LGBTQ+ community, domestic partners-no questions asked and for differently-abled and financially-dependent siblings. We also offer flexibility to port the policy even after you leave Thoughtworks.

questions.answer: Test-Driven Development (TDD) emphasizes writing tests before code to ensure functionality and improve code quality.TDD follows a cycle of Red-Green-Refactor: write a failing test (Red), make it pass (Green), then refactor the code.It encourages better design and modular code, as tests guide the development process.Example: In a project, I wrote unit tests for a new feature before implementing it, which helped identify edge cases early.TDD can lead to fewer bugs in production, as tests are created for every piece of functionality.It fosters collaboration among team members, as tests serve as documentation for expected behavior.

questions.answer: Test-Driven Development (TDD) emphasizes writing tests before code to ensure functionality and improve code quality.TDD follows a cycle of Red-Green-Refactor: write a failing test (Red), make it pass (Green), then refactor the code.It encourages better design and modular code, as tests guide the development process.Example: In a project, I wrote unit tests for a new feature before implementing it, which helped identify edge cases early.TDD can lead to fewer bugs in production, as tests are created for every piece of functionality.It fosters collaboration among team members, as tests serve as documentation for expected behavior.
